top.title: Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume
top.description: By Dickson Omobola Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District, Ali Ndume, Wednesday, admitted being part of the country’s political failure, saying government of the day is a government of some people, by some people and for some people. Ndume also lamented rising political violence in the country, saying anyone found sponsoring such acts should be held responsible. Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which public office holders were amassing wealth, saying many of them were gluttons. He said: “I am part of the failure, I cannot deny that. I am not going to claim to be the best or better than anybody. But if I had known that this is how this politics is going to turn out to be, I wouldn’t have joined it. You can compare politics to AIDS. Once you catch it, you can’t say you don’t have AIDS. I’m telling you. It’s a dangerous game, especially in Nigeria. You can’t get cured. “It’s true that government of the day has been a government of some people, by some people and for some people. If it were a government of all, this complaint and all that would not be happening. It did not start with this government. It started with the previous government. It has become a practice that you must be within the cycle. Even within the cycle, there are cabals running the government.” On violence as a tool for political competition, he said: “In fact, that is why I am happy that everybody is concerned, so that we may nip it in the bud. My friend and colleague, Ningi, moved the motion after we spoke, and I seconded the motion. Then you can see how our colleagues showed concern, and Nigerians generally. It is one of the motions that was apolitical because the problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know when it will stop, and you may have a problem putting it off. “It has also happened in a few countries where things got out of hand and, in extreme cases, reached a stage where the country’s government collapsed. You could see what happened in Bangladesh. Some years back, you could hear what happened in the Middle East. “When people easily take the law into their own hands to express their hunger and use whatever is available that can be regarded as a weapon or tool, then it becomes a dangerous thing.” Vanguard News The post Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October
top.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief ABUJA — THE Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, yesterday, shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent by Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Bawa Mokwa, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. Vanguard News The post FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: State police on verge of reality; operational guidelines bill submitted to Justice Ministry
top.description: By Henry Umoru & Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Operation of State police in Nigeria is at the verge of being realised. The National Assembly yesterday transmitted the bill ratified by the 36 state houses of Assembly to President Bola Tinubu yesterday for assent. The lawmakers asked the president to send a bill on the operational guidelines for state police for passage. Chief of Staff to president, Femi Gbajabiamila disclosed yesterday that the operational guidelines bill has been forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for validation. To quicken the process, the Senate asked President Tinubu to forward to the National Assembly the National Policing Bill which would provide for the operationlisation of state police across the 36 states of the federation for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage. It also mandated the clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana to transmit the constitutional amendment bill that seeks to establish State Police Services in Nigeria to the President for assent, having satisfied all the constitutional requirements, in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004. President Tinubu, however, received the State Police Bill later yesterday, with the Chief of Staff to the President, Mr, Femi Gbajabiamila, saying the bill requested by the Senate had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. According to him, upon receipt of the validated version, the President Working Group, which he chairs, will review and present it, alongside its report to the President for consideration. Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion, titled “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele. nigeria.title: Tompolo’s N3.6bn fleet raises questions
nigeria.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, which safeguards some of the nation’s critical oil and gas assets, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has donated over 600 vehicles estimated at about N3.68 billion to support the re-election campaign of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu across states. Tompolo, a former militant leader, doubles as the Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, a group mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election. Daily Trust reports that the cost of the vehicles has exceeded the N500 million individual donation limit under the Electoral Act 2026, but the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says the question of whether non-cash donations are covered by the law may require judicial interpretation. The vehicles constitute a series of donations committed to supporting President Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. There have also been pledges, including a promise of N10 million reward to each ward councilor in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) by the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike. The proposed reward would amount to N620 million if all 62 councillors deliver their respective wards. The material donations have renewed concerns among observers over compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act on campaign spending limits. Section 92(8) of the act provides that an individual or other entity shall not donate more than N500 million to a candidate. Under subsection (9), a candidate who knowingly contravenes the provision is liable, upon conviction, to a fine of one per cent of the permitted campaign expenditure limit, imprisonment for up to 12 months, or both. An individual who knowingly exceeds the donation limit is liable to a fine of five times the excess amount under subsection (10). Although there is no public evidence to show that Tompolo has donated sums above the N500m threshold to the Tinubu campaign, media reports revealed that he has so far distributed about 633 vehicles across at least 21 states through PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. The vehicles comprise 583 Opel Zafira wagons and 50 Sharon, with a combined market value estimated at N3.68 billion, based on average prices of fairly used vehicles of the respective models. The donations have raised questions about compliance with the electoral law and attempts by individuals to circumvent it by opting for non-cash donations. nigeria.title: Unilorin student seeks N43m for kidney transplant
nigeria.description: … Family spends over N20m, sells property to sustain treatment By Chioma Obinna The family of Olajide Victor, a 200-level student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, has appealed for N43 million to fund a kidney transplant for him after he was diagnosed with Stage V end-stage renal disease. Victor is expected to undergo the life-saving procedure at Newhaven Specialist Hospital, Lagos, as his family struggles to meet the cost of his treatment. He said his health challenges began in November 2025 after he sustained a minor fracture in his left leg while playing football at the university’s sports complex. Weeks later, his face and legs became swollen, prompting medical examinations. Following several tests, including kidney function investigations, he was diagnosed with Stage V kidney disease at Taiwo Hospital, Ilorin. A medical report signed by Dr S. Alagbe, Consultant Nephrologist, indicated that Victor requires continued haemodialysis twice weekly. His mother, Comfort Adesanya, said the family had spent over N20 million on his treatment and sold their land, house and other valuables to keep him alive. She appealed to individuals, corporate organisations and well-meaning Nigerians to help raise the N43 million required for the transplant, saying the family could no longer cope with the rising cost of treatment. Donations can be made to Victor Adekunle Olajide, UBA, Account Number: 2458216260 or call Victor on 09018866426. nigeria.title: Food security: Nigerian farmers risk wasting billions on fertilisers without soil testing, experts warn
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s quest for food security may continue to suffer setbacks unless farmers move away from indiscriminate fertiliser application and embrace soil testing and crop-specific nutrient management, agricultural experts have warned. The experts, who spoke at the 2026 South-West Nigeria Fertiliser and Soil Health Summit in Ibadan, Oyo State, cautioned that increasing fertiliser consumption without understanding the specific nutrient requirements of farmland could undermine agricultural productivity, weaken farmers’ incomes and worsen soil degradation. They argued that the country’s approach to fertiliser management must go beyond distributing inputs to farmers and focus on ensuring that the right fertiliser is applied to the right soil, for the right crop and at the appropriate time. The position formed a major highlight of the communiqué issued at the end of the summit, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, Moor Plantation, Ibadan, on Tuesday. With the theme, “Fertilisers and Food Security in South-West Nigeria: The Journey So Far,” the summit brought together more than 150 scientists, farmers, policymakers, fertiliser manufacturers and distributors, agricultural extension professionals and development partners to examine the challenges confronting fertiliser utilisation and soil health in the region. The participants expressed concern that the continued reliance on blanket fertiliser recommendations failed to address significant differences in soil fertility, acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil-related challenges across different agroecological zones. According to the communiqué, “The predominance of blanket fertiliser recommendations does not adequately address the variations in soil fertility, soil acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil constraints across different agroecological zones in the region.” The experts maintained that fertiliser recommendations should increasingly be based on soil testing, crop requirements, prevailing agroecological conditions and economically viable nutrient management practices. They also identified high fertiliser prices, inadequate distribution networks, limited access to credit and inconsistent availability as major constraints preventing smallholder farmers from accessing and effectively utilising the agricultural input. The summit further warned that declining soil organic matter, nutrient imbalance, erosion and other forms of soil degradation continued to undermine fertiliser-use efficiency and agricultural productivity. nigeria.title: 655 tribunal registrars swear oath of secrecy ahead of 2027 election cases
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri With just 58 days to the general elections, the Court of Appeal on November 16 administered the oath of secrecy to 655 clerks and Deputy Chief Registrars selected to serve on the various election tribunals. The oath was administered under the supervision of the President of the Court of Appeal (PCA), Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem. It specifically invoked the provisions of Section 1(1) of the Official Secrets Act, which concerns the protection of official information. Under the Act, a person commits an offence if they transmit classified matter to a person to whom they are not authorised, on behalf of the Government, to transmit it. The Act also provides that a person is guilty of an offence if they obtain, reproduce, or retain classified matter which they are not authorised, on behalf of the Government, to obtain, reproduce, or retain, as the case may be. The officials were warned that the oath would remain binding even after their assignments at the tribunal ended, with the PCA vowing to hand over defaulters to security agencies for prosecution. “Is there anyone among you who did not read the oath form, or who signed it and now wants to withdraw from the assignment?” Justice Dongban-Mensem asked, as the weight of the oath dawned on the officials. “I am asking because you have just signed evidence against yourselves. Anyone we find doing what we have asked you not to do will be handed over to the Police for prosecution. “I am taking all the forms you signed to the secret registry of my office, and I will lock them in my safe. In case some of you are not aware, I began my tenure as President of this Court by handing some people over for prosecution, and they were duly prosecuted. “It is because people are not made to face the consequences of their actions that we have so many problems in this country. But at the Court of Appeal, we give you every opportunity to abide by your oath, and when you don’t, we prosecute. “Some of you may be approached and asked to give details of the tribunal members’ discussions. You will start eavesdropping to get information to pass on to them. “But when you eavesdrop, you can never get the full details. That is how, before you know it, false judgments start flying around. It often comes from the registry. “We are watching you, and many other people will be watching you too. Be very careful, be committed to the nation, and let’s get it right,” the PCA warned. Election Petition Tribunals are established to hear and determine petitions arising from the conduct of elections into political offices. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, empowers the President of the Court of Appeal to constitute an Election Petition Tribunal in each State of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. nigeria.title: AI, fake voter records raise new risks for 2027 elections
nigeria.description: …Why media must not rush to publish election claims —Tech players By Juliet Umeh As Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, voters may face a new kind of deception. The society is now rife with images, videos and audios that appear authentic but have been fabricated or altered. The concern has grown after the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it removed 1,609,553 records from the voters’ register following a technical assessment. The review examined suspected multiple registrations, unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs and irregularities linked to registration transactions. INEC also found cases in which some registration personnel deliberately bypassed established procedures, including provisions for exceptional circumstances involving persons with disabilities. The commission is investigating some flagged records. The findings have prompted questions about how the irregularities occurred and whether synthetic images or other AI-generated material could be used to undermine confidence in the electoral process. There is, however, no evidence in the material available that AI-generated images caused the irregularities in the register. Olaronke Alo of the BBC Disinformation Unit while speaking on Arise Television said its initial verification found that some of the images circulating online were present in the INEC register. She said: “What we did was to do the initial verification. We went into the INEC portal and began to trace some of the names and pictures being posted on social media. We found that these images were on the INEC register.” The unit also examined claims about inconsistent records, including one instance in which the same photograph appeared against different names. Alo said it found examples of apparently incomplete or unusual names and records alleged to belong to deceased people, including former President Muhammadu Buhari. She said the unit’s task was to verify claims circulating online, rather than assess whether INEC’s response was adequate. False claims can travel fast The risks extend beyond the voters’ register. AI tools can generate convincing images, videos and audio of people appearing to say things they never said. A fabricated statement attributed to a political figure could spread rapidly before voters have time to verify it. INEC has dismissed a social media poster and accompanying text claiming the commission had reaffirmed the leadership of the African Democratic Congress. The poster carried INEC’s logo and an image of National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna. With the matter before the courts, false claims styled as official announcements could mislead the public. Other risks include political messages tailored to specific groups of voters, fabricated result sheets, screenshots purporting to show updates from INEC’s results portal, or cloned voices announcing false outcomes. nigeria.title: Army seeks land for armoured corps training in Bauchi
nigeria.description: …Commends Bala Mohammed for supporting military operations, infrastructure development By Christopher Ameh The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has appealed to the Bauchi State Government to allocate land for the establishment of a dedicated training facility for the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps in the state. Shaibu made the appeal during a courtesy visit to Governor Bala Mohammed at the Government House, Bauchi, where he commended the governor for supporting the Nigerian Army and promoting infrastructural development in the state. The Army Chief said the request had become necessary following the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, a development that had increased the number of officers and soldiers requiring specialised training. He explained that Bauchi had remained a major training centre for armoured officers, noting that military personnel usually begin their professional careers in the state through the Young Officers’ Course and other specialised programmes. According to him, armoured officers spend more than 15 years of their military careers attending various courses in Bauchi before moving to other locations as they advance in rank. He said the proposed facility would provide a dedicated centre for the continuous training of officers and soldiers throughout the year. Shaibu disclosed that the Corps Commander of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps would formally present the request to the governor, urging him to give it favourable consideration. “With this expansion, a lot of officers and soldiers have been coming into the Corps, and they will require this training consecutively throughout the year. Once that proposal comes, I crave your indulgence to please consider it,” he said. The Army Chief appreciated Mohammed for his administration’s support for the Armoured Corps, particularly the establishment of some military units in Alkaleri as part of efforts to expand the Army’s operational capacity. He also commended the governor’s infrastructural development efforts, describing the transformation of the Government House as remarkable. “Being an armoured officer myself and having started my career from here in Bauchi, I must acknowledge the massive infrastructural development taking place here. In fact, I did not recognise the Government House when I was coming,” he said. Shaibu further disclosed that he was in Bauchi to attend the grand finale of Exercise Mugunbugu, conducted in the Alkaleri general area. He described the exercise as the Nigerian Army’s major end-of-year training activity, designed to consolidate the various military exercises conducted throughout the year. The Army Chief also attended the maiden edition of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps reunion and pulling-out ceremony, which attracted more than 100 retired senior officers. He said the reunion would provide an opportunity for retired officers to reflect on their contributions to the development of the Corps and share experience

nigeria.title: Innovator develops machine to reduce drudgery in post-harvest cleaning of farm
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations. The innovation, developed by a Kogi State-born physicist and innovator, Kabir Umar, is aimed at addressing the labour-intensive and often unhygienic methods used by smallholder farmers, cleaning artisans and agro-processors to prepare agricultural commodities for local consumption and processing. Umar said the absence of affordable integrated cleaning equipment had left many small-scale operators dependent on manual sorting and washing, while those seeking mechanised alternatives often had to acquire expensive imported specialised equipment. He identified tigernuts as one of the commodities particularly affected by the challenge, explaining that some cleaning artisans still use their legs to wash the nuts before sorting them by hand. According to him, similar challenges affect the handling of other agricultural commodities, including ginger, potatoes, millet, beans and hibiscus flowers, popularly known as zobo. Umar said the idea for the machine emerged in 2020 after he ventured into agro-processing and encountered difficulties with the cleaning and drying of raw agricultural materials, which he identified as an important first step in value addition. He subsequently developed a multipurpose post-harvest sorting and washing machine, with an additional drying capability, designed to provide an integrated cleaning solution for different agricultural commodities. The innovator said he had mainly used the machine to sort and wash tigernuts for further processing into tigernut flour, adding that demonstrations to tigernut cleaning artisans showed its potential to reduce manual labour and improve productivity. He, however, disclosed that the machine was still at an advanced prototype stage and had yet to be deployed sustainably to support farmers and other operators across the agricultural value chain. According to him, wider adoption of the machine could improve the quality of agricultural produce entering local markets, support value addition, create jobs and strengthen the export potential of Nigerian commodities by improving their post-harvest handling. On the challenges facing the development, Umar identified inadequate funding as a major constraint that had slowed the transition from prototype development to commercial production. He expressed optimism that intervention through the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure’s (NASENI) Innovate Naija Challenge would help accelerate the commercialisation process. nigeria.title: Summit to examine financing, market access for farmers, agribusinesses
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja. The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected to bring together more than 1,000 farmers, agribusiness owners, investors, entrepreneurs and young Nigerians to explore opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and building sustainable businesses. The event, themed, “Unlocking Opportunities for Wealth Creation, Innovation and Sustainable Agricultural Development,” will focus on connecting agricultural producers and entrepreneurs with financing opportunities, markets, investors and business development support. A major feature of the summit will be the launch of the Wealth Creation Network, an agribusiness and entrepreneurship cooperative designed to support farmers, women and young entrepreneurs through training, access to agricultural inputs, produce aggregation, market linkages and business development services. The network is also expected to provide members with opportunities for bulk produce sales, export linkages and investment-readiness training. Speaking ahead of the event, Convener of the summit and Founder of Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, Uzua Brainz, said the initiative was intended to provide participants with practical opportunities beyond conference discussions. “We do not want people to attend Wealth Creation Summit 5.0, listen to speeches and return home exactly as they came. We want them to leave with clarity, structure, connections and practical opportunities for wealth creation,” he said. nigeria.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
nigeria.description: … Warn of burnout, stroke risks, seek healthier work environments By Chioma Obinna Health experts yesterday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. Sam Aboyeji, has charged graduating students of LIFE Theological Seminary, Ikorodu, Lagos, to uphold integrity and sound biblical doctrine as they prepare to preach the Gospel and contribute to society. Aboyeji gave the charge at the institution’s 2026 graduation ceremony, where he urged the graduands to see their graduation not as an end but as a stepping stone to greater responsibilities in God’s service. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said . Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11. Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together. How the scheme worked From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information. The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over. The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims. The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme. From Scotland to a California courtroom Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said . Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples. Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed , that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . technology.title: Chinese web giant Tencent says new US GPU ban ‘sets everyone back in China’
technology.description: The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business. “It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.” He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models. “Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.” “But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.” Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.” “And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.” Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China. Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem. But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted. “In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.” Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting. The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users. technology.title: Get ready for another critical PHP security release to drop
technology.description: Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation will release a “critical” security update on Thursday between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC. While we don’t have many details about the latest vulnerabilities – these haven’t been leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – a Wednesday advisory said the highest-severity bugs in the upcoming release are rated critical. “The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” the foundation said , urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.” We do know that one of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560. In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk. CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.” The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.” These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “ session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start() .” Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications. The November security release follows a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon , with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites. While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26. technology.title: Anthropic decides to go head-to-head with GTA VI release, schedules IPO for the same day
technology.description: Well, it’s official: Anthropic will become the first publicly-traded frontier AI lab in history come the opening of markets on Thursday. The company kicked off its IPO roadshow last week, announcing plans to offer 825 million shares with an IPO price between $70 and $78 a share when sales begin Thursday. The company's most recent SEC filing cites that price range but allows for the possibility of a higher price, which should be determined Wednesday night. Late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that Anthropic would price at $83, citing people familiar. Whatever the case, Anthropic is likely to be valued at more than $1 trillion. Anthropic’s debutante ball has been on the horizon for a while, and documents leaked in late September made it all the more inevitable as the company’s finances revved up and it sought to capture the momentum of its best quarter to date before things start to tail off. The company revised its IPO documents on November 2, warning that the 12x growth it was touting was unlikely to continue in the long term due to compute infrastructure investments to the tune of nearly $900 billion it was on the hook for over the next few years. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the revised prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." It’s possible, in other words, that Anthropic may never be a money maker despite the hype and its position as the first mover. The IPO prospectus is short on answers to critical questions and leaves a lot unanswered - like, for example, whether it’s going to actually be able to pay its bills. "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the updated prospectus admits. Investors don’t seem to care right now, though. Anthropic already has compute commitments amounting to roughly $70.7 billion in the next 12 months. That’s just shy of its $81 billion run-rate as of October 31. Expect more hot air to be injected tomorrow, adding additional surface tension and the possibility of even more losses if, and when, this monster pops. ®

technology.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
technology.description: Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register . “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million ), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 , both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.” Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concep t to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8. technology.title: To rank the world's biggest supercomputers, we're gonna need a bigger bench
technology.description: For decades, the Top500 list has tirelessly ranked the world’s biggest, most powerful, and often most unique publicly-known supercomputers. With the rise of generative AI, the list no longer lives up to its name. China’s Lineshine supercomputer at 2.2 exaFLOPS of double precision compute in the High-Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark may be the top system on the bi-annual ranking, but it’s nowhere near the biggest compute cluster in the world. Superclusters like SpaceXAI’s Colossus, Meta’s Promethius, and OpenAI’s Stargate pack hundreds of thousands of GPUs, dwarfing anything on the Top500 today. “These [companies] are not interested in submitting to the Top500,” Eth Zürich’s Torsten Hoefler said during his Supercomputing address this week. It’s a dilemma that the founders of the Top500 ranking are now grappling with. And some believe it may be time for a rethink. “What’s really needed for tracking that more appropriately is not just a different benchmark but also different methodology,” Top500 author Erich Strohmaier said. For a long time, Strohmaier explains, compute capability was roughly aligned with capacity. What happened in the last few years with AI is “capacity really pulled ahead of capability in terms of market size,” he said. “We were and we still are very focused on capability.” By capability, Strohmaier is referring to the ability to run one code across the entire cluster. “Our prime rule for benchmarking is, you have to benchmark your whole system with one code and you cannot just add two parts up to make up a number,” he explained. This is problematic for the large clusters major hyperscalers and cloud providers are now building to fuel the AI boom. “All those systems are capacity systems,” Strohmaier said. They’re not designed to run one piece of code but have instead been architected to run many, many smaller or medium-sized code instantiations, which may include training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and of course inference. Because of this, Strohmaier says, it wouldn’t be reasonable to expect SpaceXAI to run something High-Performance Linpack (HPL) on a cluster like Colossus. But these clusters are still worth tracking. They'll just need a new benchmark better suited to judging the capability of these arrays while at the same time preventing operators from gaming the system. What shape or form such a benchmark might take remains to be seen. Developing a new benchmark or methodology is no small task, and changing the existing benchmarks isn’t ideal. ”If we do anything to the benchmark itself, we’re going to lose the historic trends, which is extremely valuable,” Hoefler said. Allowing for lower precisions — HPL-MxP already does this to some extent — is one avenue for addressing the fact that these accelerators are increasingly trading FP64 performance for lower-accuracy floating-point data types like FP8 or FP4. science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. science.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. science.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. Image Credit: NASA/Michelle M. Murphy (Wyle Information Systems, LLC) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology. NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19. “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” said Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.” The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy. The competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing plan, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams. In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each. science.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. Indeed, Feedback’s history is long and storied, to the point that it would defy the efforts of even the most conscientious biographer. We have been through many incarnations, most of whom went on to do far more felicitous things with their lives. It is a little-discussed fact, one not even known to reality, that a previous Feedback helped David Foster Wallace out by composing Infinite Jest over the course of a bank holiday weekend. science.title: Are these the most spectacular and intriguing beetles in the world?
science.description: The glorious flower chafer Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum What animal is older than the dinosaurs and accounts for nearly a quarter of species on Earth? It is the magnificent beetle, an insect whose wings rest underneath a hard, protective case that often displays beautiful colours and intricate ornaments. “Wherever you stand on the land surface of the Earth save only for Antarctica, you are never more than a few metres from a beetle,” writes Maxwell Barclay in Interesting Beetles , which showcases some of their stunning variety. The main image shows the glorious flower chafer ( Howdenypa gloriosa ), a stunning opalescent green and blue. Its sleek flight from flower to flower, which takes place with the wing cases closed, unlike the clumsier flights of beetles with open wing cases, has attracted attention from aerospace engineers. They have fitted some flower chafers with tiny wireless transmitters to better understand how they manoeuvre while flying. Below is the Colorado potato beetle ( Leptinotarsa decemlineata ), which has a destructive relationship with humans. After the potato was introduced to North America, this striped beetle started to prefer spuds to native foods and quickly became a worldwide pest. Advertisement The Colorado potato beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Below, the carbuncle frog-legged beetle ( Sagra carbunculus ) shows off the buff hind legs that earned it its amphibian-inspired name and serve it well in battle – or when competing for an iridescent mate. The carbuncle frog-legged beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum The specimens in these images are taken from the archives of the Natural History Museum in London, where Barclay is senior curator in charge of beetles. It was difficult, he writes in his book, to choose which to include, “because each of the 400,000 beetle species has an interesting story to tell”. The violin beetle ( Mormolyce phyllodes ) shown below makes up for being an inelegant flyer by having a unique body shape that allows it to blend in with fallen leaves and winged seeds of trees in the steamy tropical rainforests where it resides. The violin beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Finally, the desert fog-basking beetle ( Onymacris bicolor ) shown below is another master of adaptation that can survive in places as arid and harsh as the Namib desert in southern Africa. Elegant in its black-and-white garb, this insect climbs to the top of a dune when conditions are right, points its head down and waits for dew to condense on special structures on its wings and then run into its mouth, keeping it alive. The desert fog-basking beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Barclay writes that beetles can not only survive in all these habitats, from potato fields to tropical forests and deserts, but that they are an integral part of each of them. science.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
science.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

science.title: Empire State Building Goes Gold for Voyager
science.description: NASA/Bill Ingalls The Empire State Building is seen illuminated in gold to celebrate NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft as it was about to pass one light-day away from Earth, a distance reached by no other human-made object, Nov. 17, 2026. The color gold represents the gold-plated copper phonograph record that is flying on Voyager; the Golden Record contains sounds and images selected to portray the diversity of life and culture on Earth.
